title: Active-passive DR playbook, backup/restore validation cadence, and scheduled failover drills
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and quarterly schedule for active-passive disaster recovery for Redwood Inference. Deliverables: (1) an executable DR runbook for multi-region failover that covers control plane and data plane steps, circuit-breaker and load-shedding behavior during failover, and verification checks; (2) automated and manual backup/restore validation procedures with pass/fail criteria and telemetry dashboards; (3) a recurring calendar of failover drills with scope templates (partial region, full region, control-plane-only) and post-mortem checklist. Goal is to validate that RTO and RPO targets for customer-facing hosted API and Dedicated control planes meet SLOs and to reduce mean time to recover in cross-region incidents.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A published DR runbook in Confluence with step-by-step run commands and escalation contacts; 2) Backup verification job that runs weekly and produces a green/red summary in the DR dashboard; 3) Two scheduled failover drills documented and executed in staging by the end of cycle, with post-drill writeups and action items assigned; 4) Playbook includes circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shedding policies with safe defaults and rollback steps; 5) Restore tests include data integrity checks and end-to-end smoke tests for the hosted API and Dedicated routing layers; 6) SRE and Product sign-off recorded as approvals on the Confluence page.
steps:
Overview:
1) Inventory: catalog all services, data stores, and configuration tied to region-A (primary) and region-B (secondary). Identify stateful components requiring cross-region replication (KV cache snapshots, metrics stores, model artifacts, customer keys).
2) Define SLO guardrails: map services to SLOs (availability RTO, RPO) and define target thresholds for failover and rollback (e.g., if API p99 latency > 5s for > 5min AND error rate > 3%, begin failover evaluation).
3) Circuit breakers & load shedding: set documented triggers; implement per-service levers in runtime to downgrade model flavors, enable aggressive batching, or drop non-essential routes during failover. Include safe-mode toggles in Console.
4) Backup/restore validation: implement an automated weekly job that: snapshot config + artifacts, attempt restore to an isolated "drill" namespace, run schema and checksum verification, run smoke traffic against pinned model version, and publish results to DR dashboard.
5) Failover drill plan templates: (A) Control-plane-only: exercise control-plane failover procedures without switching data plane; (B) Partial traffic shift: shift 10% traffic to secondary for 15 minutes; (C) Full region failover: switch primary->secondary with full DNS and network validation.
6) Communication and escalation: prepare run-cards, pager rotations, and Slack incident channel naming convention. Pre-authorize on-call runbook owners to approve DNS TTL changes and emergency capacity increases.
7) Post-drill: capture timeline, telemetry snapshots, action items with owners, and update playbook. Implement follow-ups as separate tickets (e.g., increase snapshot frequency, fix automation flakiness).
notes:
Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Active-passive keeps primary cold for some stateful components to reduce cross-region replication costs; trade-off is longer restore time for those components.
- For low-latency KV-cache we replicate metadata and warm critical keys during drill windows only. Full continuous replication is costly on GPU-backed caches.
- Load-shedding policy prefers 'graceful degradation' (reduce model size, increase sampling temp) over outright request rejection for paying customers; emergency rejection reserved for system-protecting thresholds.
- Security: KMS keys used for secrets are region-bound; include a step to validate key availability and an approved emergency key-rotation procedure for cross-region restores.
Known risks:
- DNS TTL propagation may cause uneven traffic shifts; include CDN-level routing tests.
- Automated restore jobs can be noisy; always run in isolated namespaces and tag metrics with drill_id.
